summary.headline: Running is on plan (127.4 of 130.4 km over weeks 1-3), but strength and cycling are lagging, week 4 started with a miss, and 1:30 is still a long way off.
observations: Weeks 1-3 volume was 42.0, 42.0 and 43.4 km against 42.0, 45.0 and 43.4 planned, so about 98% of plan. Earlier per-run review flags about CTL collapsing or being 8 of 42 km behind were written mid-week and are not borne out. CTL is 46.4 today versus 43.0 on 2 Nov, after peaking at 49.8.

Long runs have progressed 16.0, 17.0 and 18.6 km at 5:47-5:52/km with very even splits. Average HR crept from 142 to 143 to 146, and efficiency fell from 1.218 to 1.169. Easy-run HR stayed flat at 137-140, so the drift is mainly in the long runs.

Threshold work is landing: tempo blocks on 3 Nov and 17 Nov held 4:36-4:37/km at HR 162-163. The 10 Nov tempo went wrong (poor sleep, heavy legs, RPE 8, middle 3 km at 5:00/km, HR 176, stopped at 6 km). It was a sensible stop, and the next tempo was clean.

The 19 Nov reps averaged 4:00/km against a 3:55 target at HR 170-174 near max. That is close to target but costly. Tempo HR has not dropped between weeks 1 and 3, so there is no clear fitness gain yet.

Supporting work is the weak spot. Strength: 2 of 6 planned sessions (both in week 3, RPE 6-7, none in weeks 1-2). Cycling: 1 of 3 planned rides (46 min in week 2). The calf and eccentric calf work that protects your left achilles is the part being skipped.

Week 4 (the lighter week) has no logged activity: the Tue 24 Nov easy 9 km and Strength A did not happen and no reason was logged. ATL has dropped from 68 to 43 and TSB is -2.6, so you are not carrying much fatigue into Thursday.

Goal gap: your 10k of 44:00 equates to roughly a 1:37 half, and 1:30 needs 4:16/km (VDOT 51 versus 46.5). About 6.5 weeks remain and no race-pace running has been done yet. Only one run so far has an RPE, so effort is mostly read from pace and HR.
suggestions: Don't make up Tuesday's 9 km, since this is a recovery week. If you feel fine, run Thursday's 4 × 0.4 km as planned, and add a short note on why Tuesday was missed.

Fit in at least one strength session this week, prioritising the calf raises, eccentric calf raises and single-leg work. If time is tight, a 15-minute calf and glute block still helps more than skipping.
Keep Sunday's 14.6 km easy and watch the HR for that pace. If HR is still near 146 at ~5:50/km after the down week, consider holding the long run at 16-17 km rather than stepping straight back up.
Log an RPE after every key session. It makes it much easier to tell a hard day from a fitness plateau.

Treat 1:30 as a stretch rather than the base case. Use the week 5-6 interval sessions (4:09/km) and the week 8 race-pace finish as checks. If you can't hold 4:16/km comfortably for 6 km by then, consider a goal range of about 1:33-1:35 and race to it.
Before the week 7 peak (52 km, about 9 km above your current weeks), only take it on if the achilles is quiet and strength is happening at least once a week. Otherwise cap that week around 47-48 km.
